deep.reconstruction:
The page contains four short arithmetic fragments, nos. 6 (end) to 9, all about binary quadratic forms. In the transcription the letters a and α are frequently interchanged; the italic a and α are nearly identical in this typeface. The reconstruction below uses the readings that make the algebra correct.

(6a) THEOREM (composition of diagonal forms).
The two factors are (aα p² + bβ q²) and (ab r² + αβ s²).
- Expanding gives the four terms a²αb p²r², αbβ² q²s², aα²β p²s² and ab²β q²r².
- Grouping: product = αb(a²p²r² + β²q²s²) + aβ(α²p²s² + b²q²r²).
- Completing squares (the 2aαbβ·pqrs cross terms cancel): product = αb(apr ± βqs)² + aβ(αps ∓ bqr)².
- So the product has the form αb·x² + aβ·y², with x = apr ± βqs and y = αps ∓ bqr. The signs in x and y must be opposite.
- This is the previous page's Theorem 6, (ABp²+CDq²)(ACr²+BDs²) = BCx² + ADy², with the letters renamed A=a, B=α, C=b, D=β.
- The editors' cross-reference a=b=1 gives the classical case (αp²+βq²)(r²+αβs²) = α(pr±βqs)² + β(αps∓qr)².

(6b) PROBLEM: transform aα x² + bβ y² into another form 'of the same kind'.
- Substitute x = bmp + βnq and y = anp − αmq.
- The cross terms 2aαbβ·mnpq cancel, leaving aαb²m²p² + aαβ²n²q² + a²bβ n²p² + α²bβ m²q².
- Factoring: = αb m²(ab p² + αβ q²) + aβ n²(αβ q² + ab p²) = (αb m² + aβ n²)(ab p² + αβ q²).
- So the three diagonal forms [aα, bβ], [αb, aβ] and [ab, αβ] all have the same coefficient product aαbβ. Any one is a product (composition) of the other two. This is (6a) read backwards.

7. (N. Fuss) THEOREM: if x²+ny² is divisible by p²+nq², the quotient Δ is again of the form A²+nB².
- Proof attempt: assume x, y prime to p²+nq² and gcd(p,q)=1. Write x = αp+βq and y = γp+δq.
- Then x²+ny² = p²(α²+nγ²) + q²(β²+nδ²) + 2pq(αβ+nγδ), and this is set equal to Δp² + nΔq².
- Euler 'equates coefficients': Δ = α²+nγ², nΔ = β²+nδ², αβ+nγδ = 0.
- From the last: β/δ = −nγ/α. Put δ = αf, β = −nγf. Then β²+nδ² = nf²(α²+nγ²) = nΔ, so f = ±1.
- Hence x = αp ∓ nγq and y = γp ± αq. Then x²+ny² = (p²+nq²)(α²+nγ²), which is the Brahmagupta identity read backwards. So Δ = α²+nγ².

8. THEOREMS TO BE PROVED (stated, not proved).
- I: if 4na + b² is prime, it is of the form x² − a y².
- II: if 4na − b² is prime, it is of the form a y² − x².

9. THEOREM. Let p = (ma²+nb²)/Δ be a prime dividing mn f² + g². Then the quotient q = (mnf²+g²)/p is (mc²+nd²)/Δ.
- Recipe: choose λ, μ with λa − μp = ±1. Take f arbitrary and g = nλbf − νp, with ν an arbitrary integer (not introduced in the text).
- Then c = nμbf − νa and d = mμaf + νb − λΔf.
- My verification: ad + bc = μf(ma²+nb²) − λΔaf = Δf(μp − λa) = ∓Δf.
- Also mac − nbd = −ν(ma²+nb²) + nλΔbf = Δ(nλbf − νp) = Δg.
- By (ma²+nb²)(mc²+nd²) = (mac − nbd)² + mn(ad+bc)², we get Δ²pq = Δ²(g² + mnf²), i.e. pq = mnf² + g².
- p does divide mnf²+g²: modulo p, a²(n²λ²b² + mn) ≡ n(nb²+ma²) = nΔp ≡ 0, and p ∤ a.
- For prime p, the two square roots ±nλbf of −mnf² are both covered by the sign choice in λa − μp = ±1. So the recipe covers every admissible g.
- Since this is just multiplication by the conjugate, Euler is here effectively 'dividing' forms explicitly.
errors: 6a as transcribed (ab(aαp²r²+β²q²s²)+αβ(aαp²s²+b²q²r²) = ab(apr±βqs)²+αβ(αps±bqr)², form abx²+αβy²) is false. Example: a=b=α=β=p=q=r=s=1 gives LHS 4, while the RHS gives 8 or 0. The correct statement is αb(a²p²r²+β²q²s²)+aβ(α²p²s²+b²q²r²) = αb(apr±βqs)²+aβ(αps∓bqr)², of form αb x²+aβ y². This is most likely an a/α misreading in the transcription, and possibly in the print.
6a: the signs in x and y must be opposite (± and ∓). The text writes ± in both, and with the same signs the cross terms do not cancel.

6b: the grouping transcribed as abm²(...)+αβn²(...) = (abm²+αβn²)(abp²+αβq²) is wrong. The correct result is (αb m² + aβ n²)(ab p² + αβ q²). The expanded line aαb²m²p²+aαβ²n²q²+bβa²n²p²+bβα²m²q² is correct.

7: the 'equating of coefficients' of p², q², pq is unjustified, because p and q are fixed numbers, not indeterminates. The argument assumes what is to be proved: that α, β, γ, δ can be chosen so that x+y√−n = (p+q√−n)(α+γ√−n).

7: the theorem as stated (arbitrary divisor of the form p²+nq²) needs hypotheses. It is true when p²+nq² is prime: then P | (xq−yp)(xq+yp), and the Brahmagupta identity gives the quotient. In general it is not guaranteed for composite divisors when the class number exceeds 2. The redundant sentence 'Tum etiam erit...' repeats the previous one.

8 I is false in general. For a=79, n=1, b=1: 4·79+1 = 317 is prime, but 317 ≠ x²−79y². Checked by hand for y ≤ 12, which covers the Nagell bound from the fundamental unit 80+9√79. Q(√79) has class number 3, so the principal genus contains non-principal classes.

8 II is likewise false in general. For a=79, n=2, b=1: 632−1 = 631 is prime, but 79y²−x² = 631 has no solution for y ≤ 18 (the bound). Near misses: y=17 gives 22200 = 149²−1, y=18 gives 24965 = 158²+1. To be confirmed by computer.
9: the integer ν is used without being introduced; it is an arbitrary integer.

results.what: (aαp²+bβq²)(abr²+αβs²) = αb(apr±βqs)² + aβ(αps∓bqr)²: product of two diagonal binary forms with related coefficients is a third such form
results.modern_name: Composition of diagonal binary quadratic forms; generalized Brahmagupta–Euler identity
results.usually_credited_to: Euler (various papers, e.g. E256/E164 era); systematized by Lagrange (1773–75) and Gauss (Disquisitiones, 1801)

results.what: aαx²+bβy² = (αb m²+aβ n²)(ab p²+αβ q²) under x=bmp+βnq, y=anp−αmq
results.modern_name: Composition / factorization of forms with equal coefficient product (same 'genus' of convenient forms)

results.what: If p²+nq² divides x²+ny², the quotient is A²+nB² (proof by expressing x, y linearly in p, q)
results.modern_name: Euler's descent lemma: prime divisors of x²+ny² of principal form give principal quotients (divisibility in Z[√−n])
results.usually_credited_to: Euler (E228, E241 for n=1,2,3 and general statements); argument here attributed to Fuss's notes

results.what: Conjectures: prime 4na+b² is x²−ay²; prime 4na−b² is ay²−x²
results.modern_name: Euler's conjectures on prime divisors of x²−ay² (precursor of quadratic reciprocity and genus theory); strong representation form false in general
results.usually_credited_to: Euler (E164, E744); corrected and proved in genus form by Lagrange, Legendre, Gauss

results.what: Explicit formula for the quotient q=(mc²+nd²)/Δ when prime p=(ma²+nb²)/Δ divides mnf²+g², via λa−μp=±1
results.modern_name: Explicit composition/division of forms (inverse class); 'division' of a principal-form value by a represented prime

deep.surprise_reason: All material belongs to Euler's well-known study of quadratic forms and their composition. The only somewhat notable items are the fully explicit division recipe in No. 9 and the stated reciprocity-type conjectures, which are known Euler themes and in their strong form are false.
